overview.title: Welcome to Taroudant — Little Marrakech of the Souss
overview.p1: Taroudant sits in the Souss plain behind long ochre ramparts. Travellers nickname it the Little Marrakech for its walls and medina — without the imperial-city intensity. Place Assarag organises daily life; the souks and gates reward slow walking.
overview.p2: One full day covers the walls, Assarag and the markets; a second morning suits Tioute or a deeper medina wander. Stay inside or near the walls for atmosphere, or use Taroudant as a calmer base in the Souss.

q1.question: How many days in Taroudant?
q1.answer: One full day covers walls, Assarag and souks. A second day suits Tioute or a slower medina pace.

q2.question: Why “Little Marrakech”?
q2.answer: The ochre ramparts and medina silhouette recall Marrakech on a smaller, quieter Souss scale.

q3.question: How do I get to Taroudant?
q3.answer: Most visitors come by road from Agadir (about 1.5–2 hours) or Marrakech (about 3.5–4 hours).

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: Spring and autumn. Summer is very hot on the open walls; winter is mild by day and cool at night.
